> Minecraft Java snapshot: `1.21.8`  
> Protocol version: `772`  
> Source: [Java Edition protocol/Inventory](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Inventory?oldid=2999606)

Minecraft displays the **player inventory** differently, according to how the window was opened. Ranges of slot indices vary in meaning between different “windows”.

The slot number is calculated starting at 0, counting up through the window's unique slots, and then counting through the players inventory.

For all windows, the slot in the upper-left corner of the player's inventory is slot *n* where *n* is the number of unique slots, and slot number -999 is always used for clicking outside the window.

The default inventory window, which is never explicitly opened by the server, has 10 unique slots.

Rectangular regions are always indexed starting with the upper-left corner and scanning across rows. If a window has a crafting region, the output slot is always slot 0 followed immediately by the input region.

Each window type is described in the following sections. All slot index ranges are inclusive and reflect the indices observed in the Minecraft protocol.

For the window properties (additional data in each window, e.g. smelting progress or enchantments), refer to the table in the [Set Container Property](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Set_Container_Property "Java Edition protocol/Packets") packet.

Using -1 as slot index and as window id will set the cursor item (the stack dragged with the mouse).

## Player Inventory

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Inventory-slots.png/300px-Inventory-slots.png?e5b77)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Inventory-slots.png)

Inventory slots

This is the inventory window that the player can always open, typically by pressing `E` since [Beta 1.4](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Beta_1.4 "Beta 1.4"). Before, you had to press `I`.

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Ambox_warning_pn.png/32px-Ambox_warning_pn.png?b6e1c)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Ambox_warning_pn.png "File:Ambox warning pn.png")

The slots differ when storing using the [player.dat format](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Player.dat_format#Inventory_slot_numbers "Player.dat format").

| Slot range | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | crafting output |
| 1–4 | 2×2 crafting input (`1 + x + 2 * y`) |
| 5–8 | armor (head, chest, legs, feet) |
| 9–35 | main inventory |
| 36–44 | hotbar |
| 45 | Offhand slot |

### Llama

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Llama-strength5-slots.png/300px-Llama-strength5-slots.png?2af66)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Llama-strength5-slots.png)

Llama slots

The GUI that appears when interacting with a tamed [llama](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Llama "Llama") or [trader llama](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Trader_Llama "Trader Llama") that has a chest, or when opening the player's inventory while riding a tamed llama.

Depending on the value of the strength field, the number of chest rows may vary (max is 5, so 15 slots).

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Ambox_warning_pn.png/32px-Ambox_warning_pn.png?b6e1c)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Ambox_warning_pn.png "File:Ambox warning pn.png")

There still is a saddle slot, even though it cannot be used and is invisible.

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Ambox_warning_pn.png/32px-Ambox_warning_pn.png?b6e1c)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Ambox_warning_pn.png "File:Ambox warning pn.png")

Slot positions within the llama inventory vary - slot 2 may be at (1,0) or at (0,1) depending on the number of columns.

| Slot range | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | saddle |
| 1 | carpet |
| 2 - `(2 + 3 * strength)` | llama inventory |
| `(2 + 3 * strength) + 1` - `(2 + 3 * strength) + 27` | player inventory |
| `(2 + 3 * strength) + 28` - `(2 + 3 * strength) + 35` | hotbar |

- [![Unchested llama](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Llama-unchested-slots.png/120px-Llama-unchested-slots.png?e5ded)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Llama-unchested-slots.png "Unchested llama")

## Loom

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Loom-slots.png/300px-Loom-slots.png?c5ba0)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Loom-slots.png)

Loom slots

The `loom` GUI appears when interacting with a [loom](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Loom "Loom").

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/Information_icon.svg?15c1c)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Information_icon.svg "File:Information icon.svg")

The patterns retain their button ID when scrolling, i.e. the first visible button may have an ID higher than zero.

| Slot range | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | banner |
| 1 | dye |
| 2 | pattern |
| 3 | result |
| 4–30 | main inventory |
| 31–39 | hotbar |

| Button | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `n` | Pattern `n` |

## Merchant

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Merchant-slots.png/300px-Merchant-slots.png?6b2ed)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Merchant-slots.png)

Merchant slots

The `merchant` GUI appears when interacting with a [villager](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Villager "Villager") or [wandering trader](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Wandering_Trader "Wandering Trader").

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/Information_icon.svg?15c1c)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Information_icon.svg "File:Information icon.svg")

If the villager only requires one item, you can put it in either (or both) slots.

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/Information_icon.svg?15c1c)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Information_icon.svg "File:Information icon.svg")

The trade buttons are implemented using the [Select Trade](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Select_Trade "Java Edition protocol/Packets") packet.

| Slot range | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 0-1 | input items |
| 2 | result |
| 3–29 | main inventory |
| 30–38 | hotbar |

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Shulker-box-slots.png/300px-Shulker-box-slots.png?83949)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Shulker-box-slots.png)

| 27–53 | main inventory |
